:::practice What's current (2024–2026)
- **Worktrees per agent.** Claude Code documents parallel sessions in git worktrees (`claude --worktree <name>`). Cursor 2.0 (October 2025) runs up to eight agents on one prompt, each in its own worktree or on a remote machine.
- **Subagents for bounded work.** Claude Code subagents run in their own context window with their own tools and permissions. Use them for research or review that returns a result, not for writes to shared files.
- **Cloud tasks in containers.** Codex cloud tasks and similar background agents each run in a separate sandbox and return a branch or PR. The merge and its gate stay with you or CI.
- **On your laptop**: worktrees are plain git. The 0.5B workers run on CPU one after the other, so the parallelism here is logical, not wall-clock.

Sources: [Claude Code, Common workflows (worktrees)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows), [Claude Code, Subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents), [Cursor 2.0 changelog](https://cursor.com/changelog/2-0), [git worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree).
:::

:::recap What to keep from this lesson
- Delegate only independent work: disjoint paths, separate proofs, a fixed interface.
- Write the merge contract before work starts: shapes, codes, names.
- The integrator checks scope, merges in order and runs the cross-unit gate.
- Send failing units back with the finding; don't rewrite them.
- Anything a worker adds beyond the contract is a scope finding, even if it looks helpful.
:::

# Two workers in two git worktrees, then an integrator. The repo is the accounts service from 14.43-14.44. Unit
# "api" owns app/accounts.py and tests/test_accounts.py; unit "docs" owns docs/api.md; "integration" merges both
# in dependency order and runs the whole gate. Both workers are Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (CPU). The api worker samples 4
# candidates per round (up to 2 rounds) and keeps the first its own proof accepts; the docs worker writes one sentence. Run twice: once with a merge contract fixed before work starts (status
# and error code), once without it. About 2 minutes.
import json, os, pathlib, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, warnings
os.environ["HF_HUB_OFFLINE"] = "1"
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM, logging as hf_logging
from main import WorkUnit, delegation_plan, conflicts, waves
hf_logging.set_verbosity_error(); hf_logging.disable_progress_bar()
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct")
llm = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct").eval()

def chat(prompt, n=300, k=1):
    ids = tok.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], add_generation_prompt=True,
                                  return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True)["input_ids"]
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = llm.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=n, do_sample=k > 1, temperature=0.8 if k > 1 else None,
                           top_p=0.95 if k > 1 else None, top_k=None, num_return_sequences=k)
    texts = [tok.decode(o[ids.shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True) for o in out]
    return texts if k > 1 else texts[0]

def sh(cmd, cwd):
    p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, shell=isinstance(cmd, str), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    return p.returncode, (p.stdout + p.stderr).strip()

ACCOUNTS = ('"""Account service."""\n\n\ndef normalize(email: str) -> str:\n    return email.strip().lower()\n\n\n'
            'class AccountStore:\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.rows: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n'
            '    def add(self, email: str, password: str) -> None:\n        self.rows[email] = password\n\n\n'
            'def create_account(store: AccountStore, email: str, password: str) -> dict:\n    email = normalize(email)\n'
            '    store.add(email, password)\n    return {"status": 201, "email": email}\n')
TESTS = ('import unittest\nfrom app.accounts import AccountStore, create_account\n\n\nclass CreateAccountTest(unittest.TestCase):\n'
         '    def test_created(self):\n        self.assertEqual(create_account(AccountStore(), "a@b.co", "pw")["status"], 201)\n\n'
         '    def test_repeat_refused(self):\n        store = AccountStore()\n        create_account(store, "a@b.co", "pw")\n'
         '        out = create_account(store, "a@b.co", "pw")\n        self.assertEqual(out["status"], 409)\n'
         '        self.assertIn("code", out["error"])\n')
DOCS = ("# Accounts API\n\n## POST /accounts\n\nCreates an account. Returns 201 with the normalized email.\n\n"
        "## Errors\n\nAll errors use the envelope {\"error\": {\"code\", \"message\"}}.\n")
CHECK_DOCS = ("import re, sys\ncodes = set(re.findall(r'\"code\": \"(\\w+)\"', open('app/accounts.py').read()))\n"
              "doc = open('docs/api.md').read()\nmissing = sorted(c for c in codes if c not in doc)\n"
              "print('missing from docs:', missing) if missing else print('docs cover', sorted(codes))\nsys.exit(1 if missing else 0)\n")
UNITS = [WorkUnit("api", "worker-api", ("app/accounts.py", "tests/test_accounts.py"), (), "python3 -m unittest tests.test_accounts"),
         WorkUnit("docs", "worker-docs", ("docs/api.md",), (), "python3 scripts/check_docs.py"),
         WorkUnit("integration", "integrator", (), ("api", "docs"), "python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . && python3 scripts/check_docs.py")]
plan = delegation_plan(UNITS)
print(f"delegation plan: {plan['status']}   waves {plan['waves']}   conflicts {plan['conflicts'] or 'none'}\n")

def make_repo():
    root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "main"
    for path, text in {"app/__init__.py": "", "app/accounts.py": ACCOUNTS, "tests/__init__.py": "", "tests/test_accounts.py": TESTS,
                       "docs/api.md": DOCS, "scripts/check_docs.py": CHECK_DOCS}.items():
        (root / path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (root / path).write_text(text)
    for c in ("git init -q -b main", "git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=lesson add -A",
              "git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=lesson commit -qm base"):
        sh(c, root)
    return root

def worker_api(tree, contract):
    # the worker samples 4 candidates and keeps the first one its own proof accepts (up to 2 rounds)
    task = ("Make create_account refuse an email that already has an account (check `email in store.rows` after normalizing)" +
            (f": return {{\"status\": 409, \"error\": {{\"code\": \"email_taken\", \"message\": \"...\"}}}} instead of creating it."
             if contract else ". Return an error result instead of raising."))
    extra, log = "", []
    for round_ in range(1, 3):
        texts = chat(f"You own app/accounts.py:\n```python\n{ACCOUNTS}```\nTask: {task}\n{extra}"
                     "Return only the new create_account function in a ```python block.", k=4)
        for text in texts:
            m = re.search(r"```(?:python)?\n(.*?)(?:```|$)", text, re.S)
            fn = (m.group(1) if m else "").strip()
            if "def create_account" not in fn:
                log.append("no fn"); continue
            fn = fn[fn.find("def create_account"):].split("\ndef ", 1)[0].rstrip()
            (tree / "app/accounts.py").write_text(ACCOUNTS.split("def create_account")[0] + fn + "\n")
            rc, out = sh(UNITS[0].proof, tree)
            log.append(rc)
            if rc == 0:
                return log
        err = [l for l in out.splitlines() if re.match(r"^\w+(Error|Exception)\b", l)] if "out" in dir() else []
        extra = f"A previous version failed the test with: {(err or ['the test'])[-1][:150]}\nFix it. "
    return log

def worker_docs(tree, contract):
    ask = ("Write one sentence to add under '## POST /accounts' documenting what happens when the email already has an account"
           + (f": {contract}" if contract else "") + ". Mention the status code and the error code in backticks. "
           "Return only the sentence.")
    sentence = chat(f"docs/api.md:\n{DOCS}\n{ask}", n=80).strip().splitlines()[0]
    p = tree / "docs/api.md"
    p.write_text(p.read_text().replace("normalized email.\n", f"normalized email.\n\n{sentence}\n"))
    rc, out = sh(UNITS[1].proof, tree)
    return [rc], sentence

def changed(tree):
    return sh("git diff --name-only main", tree)[1].split()

RESULTS = {}
for label, contract in (("with a merge contract", 'status 409 and error code "email_taken"'), ("without one", "")):
    root = make_repo()

    print(f"   docs worker (own worktree): proof exit codes {docs_log}   changed {changed(trees['docs'])}")
    print(f"   docs sentence: {sentence[:180]!r}")
    code_names = re.findall(r'"code": "(\w+)"', (trees["api"] / "app/accounts.py").read_text())
    print(f"   error code the api worker returns: {code_names or 'none'}")
    # integrator: scope check per unit, merge in dependency order, then the cross-unit gate
    scope = {u.id: [f for f in changed(trees[u.id]) if f not in u.paths] for u in UNITS[:2]}
    for unit in waves(UNITS)[0]:
        sh(f"git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=integrator merge -q --no-edit {unit}", root)
    rc_t, out_t = sh("python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .", root)

    print(f"   gate: unit tests {'pass' if rc_t == 0 else 'FAIL'}   docs check {'pass' if rc_d == 0 else 'FAIL'} ({out_d[:60]})\n")

@@top The Parallelism Test
:::plain In plain words first
**Delegation** means handing parts of one change to separate workers, whether agents or people. It only saves time when the parts are truly independent: each worker owns files nobody else touches, has its own proof, and works to an interface fixed before anyone starts (the **merge contract**). An **integrator** then checks each handoff against its unit, merges in dependency order and runs the whole gate. Multi-agent systems and harnesses are covered in Zero to Agents 3.11 and 6.20 (linked above). This lesson runs two model workers in two real git worktrees, with and without a merge contract.

@@end Idea 5 · What the ICLR 2026 workshop treats as engineering
:::math The same idea as a formula
**Two compounding processes.** After $t$ cycles at mean rates $r_c$ and $r_a$, $C(t) \approx r_c^{\,t}$ and $A(t) \approx r_a^{\,t}$. The absolute gap and the ratio behave very differently:

$$C - A \approx r_c^{\,t} - r_a^{\,t}, \qquad \frac{C}{A} \approx \left(\frac{r_c}{r_a}\right)^{t} .$$

At matched rates the ratio stays near 1, apart from noise, while the absolute gap still wanders by an amount that grows with $C$. So a fixed absolute threshold eventually fires on noise alone in a large system, and almost never in a small one.

**A drift rule looks at the rate.** Pause when $\dfrac{(C/A)_t}{(C/A)_{t-w}} > 1 + \epsilon$. With $r_c / r_a = 1.15/1.08 = 1.065$, three cycles give $1.065^3 \approx 1.21 > 1.10$, so a 10%-in-3-cycles rule fires at cycle 3.
:::

:::worked When does each rule pause scenario A?
- Absolute rule: pause when $C - A \ge 1.5$. Since $1.15^9 - 1.08^9 \approx 3.52 - 2.00 = 1.52$, it fires around cycle 9.
- Ratio rule: pause when $C/A \ge 1.5$. Since $1.065^t \ge 1.5$ at $t = \ln 1.5 / \ln 1.065 \approx 6.4$, it fires around cycle 7.
- Drift rule: fires at cycle 3, as above.
- Earlier is safer, but the drift rule also fires on noise. In matched scenario B, it paused 93% of runs.
:::

:::check Check your mental model
- ✗ "Matched rates keep the gap bounded."  
  ✓ Over 80 cycles the absolute gap crossed 1.5 in 75% of matched runs: noise scales with size.
- ✗ "A higher mean alignment rate keeps you safe."

- ✗ "One threshold on the gap is a pause rule."  
  ✓ Decide what you measure (level, ratio or rate) and accept its false-pause cost.
- ✗ "The loop can audit itself between cycles."  
  ✓ The audit must sit outside the loop, or it becomes one more thing to optimise.
:::

# This block continues from the one above. An inter-cycle audit: instead of waiting for a large gap, check after
# every cycle how much faster capability grew than alignment, and pause when the last three cycles show a drift.
# Rule: pause if (C/A) grew by more than 10% over the last 3 cycles. Compared with the two level rules on how
# early they pause in scenario A, how often they pause in B and C, and for how many cycles. No model; a few seconds.
def drift_rule(traj, window=3, limit=1.10):
    for k in range(window, len(traj)):
        _, c0, a0, _ = traj[k - window]
        cyc, c1, a1, _ = traj[k]
        if (c1 / a1) / (c0 / a0) > limit:
            return cyc
    return None
RULES = {"abs gap >= 1.5": lambda t: first(t, lambda c, a, g: g >= 1.5),
         "ratio >= 1.5": lambda t: first(t, lambda c, a, g: c / a >= 1.5),
         "drift > 10% in 3 cycles": drift_rule}
random.seed(rsi.DEFAULT_SEED + 1)
runs = {name: [rsi.run(80, cfg) for _ in range(1000)] for name, cfg in SCEN.items()}
print(f"{'rule':<26} " + "  ".join(f"{n.split(':')[0]}: paused, median cycle" for n in SCEN))
for rname, rule in RULES.items():
    cells = []
    for sname in SCEN:
        hits = [rule(t) for t in runs[sname]]
        got = sorted(h for h in hits if h is not None)
        cells.append(f"{len(got) / 10:>5.1f}%, {got[len(got) // 2] if got else '-':>3}")
    print(f"{rname:<26} " + "        ".join(cells))
print("\nscenario A's capability/alignment ratio per cycle, on average, is r_c / r_a = "
      f"{1.15 / 1.08:.3f}: three cycles compound to {(1.15 / 1.08) ** 3:.3f}, so the drift rule fires at cycle 3")

@@end Concept
:::math The same idea as a formula
**Retry amplification.** If each call fails independently with probability $p$ and a request retries up to $r$ times, the expected calls per request are
$$E[\text{calls}] = 1 + p + p^2 + \cdots + p^{r} = \frac{1 - p^{r+1}}{1 - p}.$$
For $p = 0.1$ and $r = 3$ that is 1.11. Storms come from feedback: if load raises $p$, the sum grows toward $r + 1 = 4$ calls per request, and every layer that retries multiplies it again.

**Circuit breaker.** Open when the error rate over the last $w$ calls exceeds $\theta$; after a cooldown $T$, let one probe through (half-open) and close on success. The cooldown must be measured on the same clock as the traffic.

**Category shares.** If a trace can show several failure modes, shares computed per mode need not add up to 100% of traces, and a "per-category share" depends on how modes are counted.
:::

:::worked Reading the lesson's storm
- 200 requests made 328 calls, 1.64 per request, well below the 4 the retry cap allows.
- The service's failure rate is $0.1 + 0.02 \times \text{load}$ with load = total calls so far / 10, so it rises from 0.10 at the first request to 0.74 at the last, with or without retries.
- With the breaker, 87 requests were short-circuited and successes fell from 189 to 113.
- In this model the breaker protects a service that never recovers, so it trades 76 successes for 188 fewer calls.
:::

Within ten minutes the billing database is saturated and unrelated customers cannot log in. The post-mortem labels it "LLM hallucination". Using this lesson, what really happened, and what would you change? (Solution B1.)

# This block continues from the one above. MAST was built with human annotators and then an LLM judge. Here
# Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (CPU) labels twelve short failure reports with one of MAST's three categories, given a
# one-line definition of each, scored by the log-probability of each label. A keyword rule is the baseline.
# About 20 seconds.
import os, warnings
os.environ["HF_HUB_OFFLINE"] = "1"
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM, logging as hf_logging
hf_logging.set_verbosity_error(); hf_logging.disable_progress_bar()
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct")
llm = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct").eval()

DEFS = ("A = system design: the task, roles or stopping conditions were badly specified. "
        "B = inter-agent misalignment: agents ignored, withheld or misread each other's information. "
        "C = task verification: nobody checked the result, or the check was wrong.")
REPORTS = [
    ("The planner and the coder both thought they owned the database schema.", "A"),
    ("The agent kept repeating the same search step until it hit the turn limit.", "A"),
    ("Nobody told the agents when the task was finished, so they kept going.", "A"),
    ("The user asked for a summary in French; the prompt never mentioned the language.", "A"),
    ("The researcher found the API was deprecated but did not tell the coder.", "B"),
    ("The coder ignored the reviewer's comment and merged anyway.", "B"),
    ("Agent B answered a different question from the one agent A asked.", "B"),
    ("Halfway through, the conversation was reset and the agents lost the plan.", "B"),
    ("The tester said all tests passed, but the tests never ran.", "C"),
    ("The final answer had an arithmetic error that no agent checked.", "C"),
    ("The verifier only checked that the code compiled, not that it was correct.", "C"),
    ("The report was marked done without comparing it with the requirements.", "C"),
]
def label_scores(text):
    p = f"{DEFS}\nFailure report: {text}\nWhich category is it, A, B or C?"
    ids = tok.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": p}], add_generation_prompt=True,
                                  return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True)["input_ids"]
    pre = tok("Category", return_tensors="pt")["input_ids"]
    with torch.no_grad():
        lg = llm(torch.cat([ids, pre], 1)).logits[0, -1]
    return {c: lg[tok.encode(" " + c)[0]].item() for c in "ABC"}
KEYWORDS = {"A": ("owned", "specif", "repeat", "finished", "prompt", "role"),
            "B": ("tell", "ignored", "different question", "lost", "misread"),
            "C": ("check", "verif", "test", "passed")}
def keyword(text):
    t = text.lower()
    for c in "ABC":
        if any(k in t for k in KEYWORDS[c]):
            return c
    return "?"
raw = [label_scores(t) for t, _ in REPORTS]
mean = {c: sum(r[c] for r in raw) / len(raw) for c in "ABC"}            # calibrate: remove each label's average pull
model_raw = [max(r, key=r.get) for r in raw]
model_cal = [max("ABC", key=lambda c: r[c] - mean[c]) for r in raw]
for (t, truth), a, b in zip(REPORTS, model_raw, model_cal):
    print(f"   true {truth}  keyword {keyword(t)}  model {a}  calibrated {b}   {t[:62]}")
gold = [g for _, g in REPORTS]
print(f"\ncorrect of 12: keyword rule {sum(keyword(t) == g for t, g in REPORTS)}, model {sum(a == g for a, g in zip(model_raw, gold))}, "
      f"calibrated model {sum(b == g for b, g in zip(model_cal, gold))}")
print(f"labels the raw model used: { {c: model_raw.count(c) for c in 'ABC'} }")

It never reaches 4, the cap, because most requests still succeed early.

Every layer retried on its own: 5 refund attempts, each re-checked 3 times by billing, plus tickets re-opened by intake, so one failed refund could become dozens of calls. The billing database took the multiplied load, and it was shared with login, so the outage spread to customers who never touched refunds. No model output was wrong; this is a coordination and system-design failure.

**What to change:**
- **Retry budgets per request** across all layers, with backoff and jitter, and only one layer allowed to retry a given call.
- **Circuit breakers** on the payment provider and on billing, failing fast with a "refund pending" status.

@@top Problem
:::plain In plain words first
Multi-agent systems fail often, and in recognisable ways. **MAST** is a taxonomy of those failures from 1,642 real traces: badly specified tasks and roles, agents that misread or ignore each other, and results nobody checks. Other failures come from agents being too alike (**monoculture**, **conformity**) and from errors that spread from one service to the next (**cascades**), which **circuit breakers** contain. Specs, contracts and failure modes for a single production agent are covered in Zero to Agents 12.2 (linked above). This lesson measures the lesson's retry-storm simulator and breaker, and tries a small model as a MAST annotator.
:::
@@

Three root categories: **Specification Problems** (41.77%) — role ambiguity, unclear task definitions; **Coordination Failures** (36.94%) — communication breakdowns, state desync; **Verification Gaps** (21.30%) — missing validation, absent quality checks. @@end Idea 4 · Refuse to advance without feedback
:::math The same idea as a formula
**Cost of feedback.** With $r$ retries per task and a feedback message of $f$ tokens, a task's prompt cost grows by about $r \cdot f$. A raw log of $L$ lines costs $f \propto L$; a head-and-tail record costs $f \propto h + t$, fixed whatever the log length.

**Exposure.** If a secret appears in the output with probability $s$ per run and feedback is sent raw, the chance that at least one of $n$ prompts contains it is $1-(1-s)^n$; redaction before the model sees the text makes it 0 for the patterns it covers.

**Advance rule.** A step may be marked passed or failed only if an exit code $e$ exists: $\text{advance} \iff e \neq \text{null}$. A timeout is not a failure of the code; it is a missing measurement.
:::

:::worked Three kinds of feedback on the same bugs
- Five bugs, three attempts each, tests that print 200 debug lines and a fake API key before the assertion.
- Fixes stay at one or two of five in every mode, and vary by one between runs: this model cannot use richer feedback well.
- Prompt tokens differ several-fold: "the test failed" adds almost nothing; the raw log adds thousands of tokens of debug noise; the record adds the head, tail and the assertion line.
- The raw log carried the API key into the model's prompt; the record replaced it with `[REDACTED]`. A hanging test produced `exit_code=None`, and `loop_can_advance` refused to count it as anything.
:::

:::check Check your mental model
- ✗ "More output gives the agent more to work with."  
  ✓ Here it added thousands of tokens and no fixes.
- ✗ "Logs are internal, so secrets in them are harmless."  
  ✓ Whatever goes into feedback goes into the prompt, and into traces.
- ✗ "A timeout means the test failed."  
  ✓ It means nothing was measured; do not advance.
- ✗ "Truncation can be random to save space."  
  ✓ Keep it deterministic so the same run gives the same record.
:::

:::predict Predict before you run
The same five bugs are retried with three kinds of feedback: "the test failed", the whole raw log (200 debug lines, a fake API key, then the assertion), or the lesson's feedback record. Which mode fixes the most bugs? Which costs the most tokens, and which leaks the key? (Solution P1.)

@@top The problem
:::plain In plain words first
**Runtime feedback** is what the agent learns from actually running something: the exit code, the output, how long it took. Raw output is a poor message, though: long logs bury the one line that matters, cost tokens, and can carry secrets into the prompt. @@end Concept
:::math The same idea as a formula
**Exactly-once effect.** Delivery is at least once, so a step may run $k \ge 1$ times. A side effect $e$ applied with key $\kappa$ is idempotent if
$$\text{apply}(e, \kappa)^{k} = \text{apply}(e, \kappa) \quad \text{for all } k \ge 1.$$
The key must be stable across retries, for example (run id, step number), not a fresh random id per attempt.

**Checkpoint growth.** If state is an append-only list that gains about $d$ bytes per step, the full snapshot after step $t$ is about $t\,d$, and storing every snapshot costs
$$\sum_{t=1}^{T} t\,d = \tfrac{T(T+1)}{2}\,d,$$
against $T\,d$ for deltas. The ratio, $(T + 1)/2$, grows with the length of the run.
:::

:::worked A charge that happens twice
- Steps are numbered 1 to 3. Step 2 of run-7 bills the customer 10, then the worker crashes before writing the checkpoint for step 2.
- The last checkpoint is step 1, so the new worker re-runs step 2 and bills 10 again.
- Total billed: 40 for three steps of 10, while the checkpoint says 30.
- With the key (run-7, 2) recorded by the payment service, the retry is recognised and the total is 30.

# This block continues from the one above. A small real agent on the lesson's CheckpointStore: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
# (sampled, temperature 0.8, CPU) writes an 8-step trip plan, one short step per super-step, and the full message
# history is checkpointed after every step, as LangGraph does by default. We measure how the checkpoints grow,
# then crash after the model call in step 4 and resume, once re-calling the model and once replaying a journal of
# recorded model outputs. About 1 minute.
import os, json, tempfile, warnings
os.environ["HF_HUB_OFFLINE"] = "1"
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM, logging as hf_logging
hf_logging.set_verbosity_error(); hf_logging.disable_progress_bar()
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct")
llm = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct").eval()

def llm_step(messages, seed):
    ids = tok.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True)["input_ids"]
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = llm.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=40, do_sample=True, temperature=0.8, top_k=0, top_p=1.0)
    return tok.decode(out[0, ids.shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True).strip()

STEPS = 8
observed = {}
def run(store, journal, crash_at=None, seed_base=0):
    last = store.latest("trip")
    step, state = (last[0] + 1, last[1]) if last else (0, {"messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You plan a 2-day trip to Lisbon, one short step at a time."}]})
    while step < STEPS:
        msgs = state["messages"] + [{"role": "user", "content": f"Step {step + 1} of {STEPS}: one sentence."}]
        key = f"trip:{step}"
        if journal is not None and key in journal:
            reply = journal[key]                              # replay the recorded model output
        else:
            reply = llm_step(msgs, seed=seed_base + step)
            observed[key] = reply                             # what the model said, for the comparison below
            if journal is not None:
                journal[key] = reply                          # in production the journal is durable, like the checkpoint
        if step == crash_at:
            raise RuntimeError("crash after the model call, before the checkpoint")
        state = {"messages": msgs + [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply}]}
        store.write("trip", step, state); step += 1
    return state

f = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".db", delete=False); f.close()
store = CheckpointStore(f.name)
run(store, journal=None)
rows = store.conn.execute("SELECT super_step, length(state_json) FROM checkpoints WHERE thread_id='trip' ORDER BY super_step").fetchall()
sizes = [n for _, n in rows]; deltas = [sizes[0]] + [b - a for a, b in zip(sizes, sizes[1:])]
print(f"checkpoint sizes per step (bytes): {sizes}")
print(f"total stored: {sum(sizes)} bytes as full snapshots, {sum(deltas)} as deltas ({sum(sizes) / sum(deltas):.1f}x)")
os.unlink(f.name)

print("\ncrash after the model call in step 4, then resume on a new worker")
for name, journal in (("re-call the model", None), ("replay the journal", {})):
    f = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".db", delete=False); f.close(); store = CheckpointStore(f.name)
    observed.clear()
    try:
        run(store, journal, crash_at=3, seed_base=100)
    except RuntimeError:
        pass
    before = observed["trip:3"]
    final = run(store, journal, seed_base=900)                # the new worker's sampler starts from a different seed
    after = final["messages"][8]["content"]
    print(f"   {name:19s} same step-4 text as before the crash: {before == after}")
    print(f"      before: {before[:80]!r}")
    print(f"      after:  {after[:80]!r}")
    os.unlink(f.name)

T["R2"] = r"""
**The crash billed the customer twice for one step.** Without a dedup key the total was 40 for three steps of 10, while the checkpoint said 30: step 2's charge ran before the crash and again on resume. With the key (run, step), the retry was ignored and the total was 30.

A plain `INSERT` on the same primary key raised an `IntegrityError`, which is the behaviour you want; a lease would stop the second worker from starting at all.

**The queue handles one message per three steps.** Six messages took 18 steps, because each message goes through processing and response on its own. MegaAgent's Processing state batches everything queued into one model call.

**Threads cost memory, but less than the lesson says.** 2,000 waiting threads added 31 MB resident, about 16 KB each, and reserved 17 GB of virtual memory for their stacks. 2,000 asyncio tasks added about 1 MB.
"""
T["R3"] = r"""
**Snapshots grow with the run.** Each checkpoint holds the whole history, from 322 bytes after step 1 to 2,229 after step 8. Storing all eight took 9,973 bytes against 2,229 as deltas, 4.5 times more after only 8 steps. The ratio keeps growing, which is why LangChain's 200-turn workload went from 5.3 GB to 129 MB with deltas.

**Re-calling a sampled model changes the run.** After the crash in step 4, the new worker called the model again and got a different sentence ("Be sure to check the weather forecast") from the one the crashed worker had produced ("Don't miss out on exploring the city"). Anything downstream that already saw the first version now disagrees with the record.

**Replaying the journal keeps the run consistent.** With model outputs recorded as they are produced, the resumed worker reused the original text. That is what Temporal does with activity results; for agents, record every model and tool result with its step.
"""
T["SP1"] = r"""
**40.** The last checkpoint is step 1, so the new worker re-runs step 2 from the start and bills again. The run did 30 of work, the checkpoint says 30, and the customer paid 40. The same happened in the run above. A key of (run id, step), checked by the payment service, turns the second charge into a no-op.
"""
T["SB1"] = r"""
**Duplicate emails.** Retries re-run every step after the last checkpoint, including the send. Fix: an idempotency key per (run, step) on the email call, or an outbox table that a separate sender drains exactly once.

**Contradictory sections.** A resumed run calls the model again for the step it was on, gets a different sample, and continues from text that earlier steps or other workers never saw. Concurrent retries without a lease can also interleave two workers on one run. Fix: journal every model and tool output with the step, replay them on resume, and hold a lease per run.

**400 GB of checkpoints.** Full snapshots of a growing history cost storage roughly quadratic in run length. Fix: store deltas with periodic full snapshots, expire old checkpoints after a run completes, and keep large artifacts out of the state.
"""

            if step == crash_after_charge_at:
                raise RuntimeError("crash between the side effect and the checkpoint")
            state["billed"] += 10; store.write("run-7", step, dict(state)); step += 1
    try:
        worker(crash_after_charge_at=1)
    except RuntimeError:
        pass
    worker()
    print(f"   dedup key {'on ' if dedup else 'off'}: customer charged {sum(charges)} for 3 steps of 10 (checkpoint says {store.latest('run-7')[1]['billed']})")
    os.unlink(path)

print("\n2. two workers resume the same thread at once (no lease)")
path = db(); s1, s2 = CheckpointStore(path), CheckpointStore(path)
s1.write("t-9", 0, {"notes": ["plan"]})
step_a, st_a = s1.latest("t-9"); step_b, st_b = s2.latest("t-9")
s1.write("t-9", step_a + 1, {"notes": st_a["notes"] + ["worker A: searched papers"]})
s2.write("t-9", step_b + 1, {"notes": st_b["notes"] + ["worker B: drafted intro"]})
print(f"   final state: {s1.latest('t-9')[1]}; worker A's step was overwritten without an error (INSERT OR REPLACE)")
conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
try:
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO checkpoints VALUES (?, ?, ?)", ("t-9", 1, "{}")); conn.commit()
except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:
    print(f"   a plain INSERT would have refused the second write: IntegrityError: {e}")
os.unlink(path)

print("\n3. the per-agent queue: one message per three steps")
q = AgentQueue("agent-a")
for i in range(6):
    q.enqueue({"task": i})
steps = 0
while q.in_queue or q.state != AgentState.IDLE:
    q.step(); steps += 1
print(f"   6 messages took {steps} steps; each pass through processing handles one message (MegaAgent batches the queue)")

print("\n4. what 2,000 waiting threads and 2,000 waiting tasks cost")
def mem():
    d = dict(l.split(":", 1) for l in open("/proc/self/status") if l.startswith(("VmRSS", "VmSize")))
    return int(d["VmRSS"].split()[0]) / 1024, int(d["VmSize"].split()[0]) / 1024
r0, v0 = mem()
stop = threading.Event()
ths = [threading.Thread(target=stop.wait) for _ in range(2000)]
t0 = time.perf_counter()
for t in ths:
    t.start()
t_start = time.perf_counter() - t0
r1, v1 = mem(); stop.set()
for t in ths:
    t.join()
print(f"   threads: started in {t_start:.2f} s; resident memory +{r1 - r0:.0f} MB, virtual +{v1 - v0:.0f} MB "
      f"(+{(r1 - r0) * 1024 / 2000:.0f} KB resident each)")
async def tasks():
    ev = asyncio.Event(); ra, va = mem()
    ts = [asyncio.create_task(ev.wait()) for _ in range(2000)]
    await asyncio.sleep(0); rb, vb = mem(); ev.set(); await asyncio.gather(*ts)
    return rb - ra, vb - va
dr, dv = asyncio.run(tasks())
print(f"   asyncio tasks: resident memory +{dr:.0f} MB, virtual +{dv:.0f} MB")

@@top Problem
:::plain In plain words first
In production, agent runs last minutes or hours, workers crash, and load spikes. **Durable execution** saves each run's state after every step (a **checkpoint**), so any worker can pick the run up where it stopped. Two more things make that safe: side effects that can be repeated without harm (**idempotency**), and only one worker owning a run at a time (a **lease**). Durable execution, scaling and multi-agent platforms are covered in Zero to Agents 12.8, 12.9 and 12.17 (linked above). This lesson breaks the lesson's checkpoint store in the two ways production does, measures what threads cost, and checkpoints a small real agent.
:::

@@end Idea 6 · Where vendor writeups stop short
:::math The same idea as a formula
**Two rates that a workbench changes differently.** Over $n$ runs, let $c$ be the fraction actually completed and $f$ the fraction that claim success while failing (false "done"). What a user experiences is roughly
$$\text{trusted outcomes} = c, \qquad \text{silent failures} = f.$$
A verification gate drives $f$ towards 0 by refusing any finish whose checks fail. It cannot raise $c$ by itself; that takes a model able to do the work, plus feedback it can use.

**Retry budget.** With a gate, an agent that fixes the task with probability $q$ per attempt and has $k$ attempts finishes with probability $1-(1-q)^k$. If $q = 0$, every extra attempt is spent being rejected.
:::

:::worked Reading the five-task table
- Prompt-only: 0 of 5 fixed, and 2 of 5 runs called `finish` on code that still failed its test (is_even and to_fahrenheit): $c = 0$, $f = 0.4$.
- Workbench: 0 of 5 fixed, 0 false finishes: $c = 0$, $f = 0$. The gate rejected 12 premature finishes across three tasks.
- So the workbench removed every false "done" and added no fixes: in all twelve runs of this lesson the model never called `write_file`.
- In production terms: without the gate, 2 of 5 tickets would have been closed as fixed while broken; with it, all 5 stay visibly open for a person or a stronger model.
:::

:::check Check your mental model
- ✗ "A good prompt is a workbench."  
  ✓ A prompt asks; the gate, the scope check and the test runner enforce.
- ✗ "A workbench makes a weak model capable."  
  ✓ It stopped every false 'done' and produced no fixes.
- ✗ "If the agent says it finished, check its summary."  
  ✓ Run the tests and the scope check; ignore the summary.
- ✗ "Swapping in a better model removes the need for a workbench."  
  ✓ Same model, different harness, moved one agent from outside the top 30 to the top 5.
:::

:::predict Predict before you run
A 0.5B model must fix `is_even` (it returns `n % 2 == 1`) using file tools, and must call a tool every turn, `finish` included. With no workbench, what will it do? With a workbench whose gate runs the tests on every `finish`? (Solution P1.)

:::practice What's current (2024–2026)
- **"Harness engineering"** became the common name in 2026 for this work: Anthropic's long-running-agent guidance, OpenAI's Codex harness writing, LangChain's deep-agents work and Martin Fowler's site all describe instruction files, tool design, feedback loops and verification around a fixed model.
- **Measured effects**: LangChain reports a 13.7-point Terminal Bench 2.0 gain from harness changes alone with the model fixed; vendor case studies (tool pruning, verification steps) report similar jumps. Treat single-vendor numbers as directional.
- **Coding agents in practice** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) ship most of the seven surfaces: instruction files such as `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, permission and scope settings, hooks that run checks, subagents for review, and session state.
- **On your laptop**: this harness is about 100 lines of Python around any model. Rerun it with a 3B to 7B coder model in 4-bit on the RTX 4060 to see the gate turn rejections into fixes.

Sources: [LangChain, Improving Deep Agents with harness engineering (Feb 2026)](https://www.langchain.com/blog/improving-deep-agents-with-harness-engineering), [Anthropic, Effective harnesses for long-running agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents), [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md/).
:::

:::recap What to keep from this lesson
- A workbench is the system around the model: instructions, scope, feedback, verification, review, state, handoff.
- Verification gates stop false "done" claims; they do not add capability.
- Judge an agent by checks you run, not by what it says it did.
- Report fixes and false claims separately.
- Keep the surfaces when you swap the model.
:::

k31/V2.py:
# The same coding task under two harnesses, with a real model. A tiny repo has a bug in app.py and a test
# file. Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (greedy, CPU) must call a tool every turn: read_file, write_file or finish. Prompt-only:
# just the task. Workbench: the task plus scope (allowed files), a run_tests tool that returns real output, and
# a verification gate that runs the tests and the scope check whenever the agent says it is finished, and
# sends failures back. Each run is reported with the lesson's RunResult and failure_report (code/main.py).
import json, os, pathlib, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, warnings
os.environ["HF_HUB_OFFLINE"] = "1"
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM, logging as hf_logging
from main import RunResult, failure_report
hf_logging.set_verbosity_error(); hf_logging.disable_progress_bar()
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct")
llm = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct").eval()

REPO = {
    "app.py": 'def is_even(n):\n    """Return True if n is even."""\n    return n % 2 == 1\n',
    "test_app.py": "import unittest\nfrom app import is_even\n\nclass T(unittest.TestCase):\n    def test_even(self):\n"
                   "        self.assertTrue(is_even(4))\n    def test_odd(self):\n        self.assertFalse(is_even(7))\n\n"
                   "if __name__ == '__main__':\n    unittest.main()\n",
    "README.md": "# demo\nVersion 1\n", "scripts/release.sh": "echo release\n",
}
TASK = ("is_even in app.py returns the wrong answer. Fix it by writing the corrected app.py.\napp.py now contains:\n"
        + REPO["app.py"])
ALLOWED = ["app.py"]

def fn(name, desc, **params):
    return {"type": "function", "function": {"name": name, "description": desc, "parameters": {
        "type": "object", "properties": {k: {"type": "string"} for k in params}, "required": list(params)}}}
BASE_TOOLS = [fn("read_file", "Read a file.", path="file path"),
              fn("write_file", "Replace a file's whole content.", path="file path", content="new full content"),
              fn("finish", "Say the task is complete.", message="short summary")]
TEST_TOOL = fn("run_tests", "Run the test suite and return its output.")

def make_repo():
    root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    for name, body in REPO.items():
        (root / name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (root / name).write_text(body)
    return root

def run_tests(root):
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", "-q", "test_app"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    return p.returncode == 0, (p.stdout + p.stderr).strip()[-400:]

def model_turn(msgs, tools):
    """One model step, constrained to start a tool call (tool_choice="required"): finish is a tool too."""
    ids = tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tools=tools, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True)["input_ids"]
    prefix = '<tool_call>\n{"name": "'
    ids = torch.cat([ids, tok(prefix, return_tensors="pt")["input_ids"]], dim=1)
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = llm.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=200, do_sample=False)
    text = prefix + tok.decode(out[0, ids.shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)
    calls = []
    for blob in re.findall(r"<tool_call>\s*(\{.*?\})\s*</tool_call>", text, re.S):
        try:
            d = json.loads(blob); calls.append((d["name"], d.get("arguments", {}) or {}))
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError):
            pass
    return calls, text

def agent(workbench, max_turns=8):
    root = make_repo()
    result = RunResult(label="workbench" if workbench else "prompt-only",
                       surfaces_present=["instructions", "scope", "feedback", "verification"] if workbench else [])
    tools = BASE_TOOLS + ([TEST_TOOL] if workbench else [])
    system = "You are a coding agent working in a small Python repo. Use the tools."
    if workbench:
        system += (f" You may change only these files: {', '.join(ALLOWED)}. Done means: the tests in test_app.py pass "
                   "(use run_tests) and no other file changed. Call finish only when that is true.")
    msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": TASK}]
    for _ in range(max_turns):
        calls, text = model_turn(msgs, tools)
        if not calls:
            msgs += [{"role": "assistant", "content": text}, {"role": "user", "content": "Use a tool."}]
            continue
        msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": n, "arguments": a}} for n, a in calls]})
        finished = False
        for name, args in calls:
            ACTIONS.setdefault(result.label, []).append(name if name != "write_file" else f"write_file({args.get('path')})")
            path = str(args.get("path", "")).lstrip("./")
            if name == "read_file":
                out = (root / path).read_text() if (root / path).is_file() else "error: no such file"
            elif name == "write_file":
                (root / path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (root / path).write_text(str(args.get("content", "")))
                result.files_touched.append(path); out = f"wrote {path}"
            elif name == "run_tests" and workbench:
                result.tests_run = True; ok, out = run_tests(root); out = ("PASS\n" if ok else "FAIL\n") + out
            elif name == "finish":
                result.declared_success = True; finished = True
                if workbench:                                   # the verification gate
                    ok, log = run_tests(root)
                    off = [f for f in result.files_touched if f not in ALLOWED]
                    if ok and not off:
                        out = "verified"
                    else:
                        finished = False; result.declared_success = False
                        out = "rejected by the verification gate: " + ("tests fail: " + log[-200:] if not ok else "") + \
                              (f" files outside scope changed: {off}" if off else "")
                        result.notes.append("gate rejected a finish")
                else:
                    out = "ok"
            else:
                out = f"error: unknown tool {name}"
            msgs.append({"role": "tool", "content": out})
        if finished:
            break
    result.actually_passing = run_tests(root)[0]
    final = (root / "app.py").read_text().strip().splitlines()[-1].strip()
    return result, final

    print(f"  actions: {', '.join(ACTIONS.get(res.label, []))}")

k31/head.md:
@@top The problem
:::plain In plain words first
A **workbench** (people also say **harness**) is everything around the model while it works: the instructions it starts with, the files it may touch (**scope**), real output from the commands it runs (**feedback**), a check that must pass before "done" counts (**verification**), and notes that let the next session continue (**state** and **handoff**). The model decides; the workbench decides what the model sees and what it may claim. The usual failure without one is an agent that says it finished when nothing works. This lesson gives a small model the same bug-fix tasks with and without a workbench and counts real fixes and false "done"s.
:::
@@
